title: Two independent Discord (and two Pushover) configurations on the same page; filling one leaves the other's Test saying it is unconfigured
what_happened: The Notifications page has a 'Discord' section near the top (Webhook URL + Test Discord) and a 'Discord (routing matrix)' section ~2000px lower (Webhook URL + Username override + Save + Test). They are separate stores. I pasted https://discord.com/api/webhooks/111/AUDITMATRIX into the routing-matrix one and saved -- toast 'Discord (routing) saved', field became '******** (stored securely)' with Replace/Clear. I then scrolled back up: the top 'Discord' section's Webhook URL was still the empty placeholder, and its 'Test Discord' answered 'Please enter a Discord webhook URL'. The identical duplication exists for Pushover ('Pushover' with API Key/User Key/Test vs 'Pushover (routing matrix)' with API token/User key/Device/Save/Test).
expected: One Discord configuration per page. A user who configures Discord anywhere on the Notifications page should not be told by another control on that same page that Discord is unconfigured. If the legacy rows must survive for the legacy push path, they need to read from the same secret and be labelled as such.
repro: Settings > NOTIFICATIONS & REMOTE > Notifications. Scroll to 'Discord (routing matrix)', paste any webhook URL, press 'Save Discord config'. Scroll back up to the 'Discord' section and press 'Test Discord'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-52-discord-saved.png (routing matrix saved, masked), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-56-legacy-discord4.png (top Discord section still empty), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-57-legacy-discord-test.png ('Please enter a Discord webhook URL'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-47-tr-2.png (duplicate Pushover). DB: app_settings discord_webhook='' while notification_transport_discord={"webhookUrl":"",...} with the URL in the keyring.
proposed_fix: Delete the legacy Discord/Pushover rows from notification_settings.dart and migrate discord_webhook / pushover_key / pushover_user into the keyring-backed transport config on first run (the same one-shot migration pattern already used by secrets_store.dart's notification_secrets_migrated_v2). If they must stay, retitle them 'Discord (legacy push)' and have both read the same source.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. On one scroll of the Notifications page I see 'Discord' (Webhook URL + Test Discord) at notification_settings.dart:587-623 reading settings.discordWebhook, and 'Discord (routing matrix)' at notification_routing_settings/discord_transport_section.dart:34/64 backed by the keyring transport config — plus the identical pair for 'Pushover' (notification_settings.dart:624-677) vs 'Pushover (routing matrix)' (pushover_transport_section.dart:37/80). The duplication is deliberate per the in-source comment at notification_settings.dart:678-683 ('separate keys to keep legacy NotificationService working unchanged'), but nothing in the UI says so. Live contradiction on ONE page: the routing-matrix Discord webhook showed '******** (stored securely)' with Replace/Clear (shot sov-30-disc2.png) while the top 'Discord' section's Webhook URL was the empty grey hint, and pressing its 'Test' produced the orange toast 'Please enter a Discord webhook URL' (shot sov-34-crop.png). Confirmed. I am lowering P1 -> P2: unlike finding #1 nothing is silently dropped on a path the user armed — both halves work in isolation, the harm is a duplicated/contradictory config surface. (Incidental, worth its own item: the routing-matrix secret was already present on a --fresh profile, i.e. the keyring is not scoped by SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR and leaks across audit profiles.)

title: Auto-Save Status reports 'Last backup: Never' while a backup from 20 minutes earlier in the same session exists and is listed on another settings page
what_happened: Fresh profile launched 13:54:14Z. At 14:19Z the Status card read 'Last backup: Never' with trailing state 'Pending'. At that exact moment app_settings held autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-01T13:59:15.750118Z, and Settings > ADVANCED > Backup & Restore listed seven real bundles (skotiq_autosave_2026-08-01T09-59-20 ... T10-09-50 local) which also exist on disk in ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups/. After pressing 'Back Up Now' the same card immediately read '0s ago / In 23h', and later '18m ago / In 23h' -- so the widget only shows backups it observed after subscribing, and never hydrates the persisted timestamp.
expected: 'Last backup: 20m ago'. Telling an operator their database has NEVER been backed up when it was backed up 20 minutes ago is the kind of false negative that makes people either panic-export or stop trusting the field.
repro: Start the app on a fresh profile. Wait ~5 min for the startup auto-backup. Open Settings > Files & Storage > scroll to AUTO-SAVE & BACKUPS > Status. Compare with `sqlite3 <profile>/data/skotiq.db "select value from app_settings where key='autosave.last_backup_at'"` and with Settings > ADVANCED > Backup & Restore > Recent Backups.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-60-autosave.png and settings-obs-61-savenow.png ('Never' / 'Pending'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-62-backupnow.png ('0s ago' after manual backup), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-81-testconn2.png (Recent Backups list, 7 bundles from 09:59-10:20), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-92-autosave-recheck.png ('18m ago')
proposed_fix: The hydrating provider already exists -- packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/auto_save_service.dart:745-780 defines an autoSaveStatusStream that back-fills lastBackup from the persisted _lastBackupKey. Have _AutoSaveSettingsState watch that provider instead of ref.read(autoSaveServiceProvider).status / .statusStream.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced independently on a fresh profile. Profile launched 14:48:29Z; the startup auto-backup ran at 14:53:25Z (app_settings autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-01T14:53:25.161687Z, and ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups/skotiq_autosave_2026-08-01T10-53-25.082618.nsbackup exists on disk). At 14:56Z Settings > Files & Storage > AUTO-SAVE & BACKUPS > Status still read 'Last backup / Never' with trailing 'Pending' (shot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sov-04-autosave2.png). The named cause is right: _AutoSaveSettingsState.initState reads ref.read(autoSaveServiceProvider).status and subscribes to .statusStream (auto_save_settings.dart:41-56), which never back-fills the persisted key. The strongest evidence is an in-app contradiction the finding only half-states: Settings > ADVANCED > Backup & Restore on the SAME running instance showed 'Last Full Backup: Aug 1, 2026 10:53' (shot sov-39-backuprestore.png) because backup_screen.dart:432 watches autoSaveStatusProvider — the hydrating provider at auto_save_service.dart:762 that the finding points at (it names it 'autoSaveStatusStream'; the actual identifier is autoSaveStatusProvider, doc comment at 745-761 — a naming slip, not a defect in the claim). The proposed fix is exactly the pattern already used by the sibling screen. Lowering P1 -> P2: it is a display-only false negative on one of two surfaces; no data is lost and no night is at risk.

title: Editing a settings dropdown fires a CRITICAL 'Safe the rig' alert on a completely idle app, and the alert text contradicts itself
what_happened: With no devices connected, no run active and the app sitting on the Settings screen, flipping Weather Safety > 'Enable weather safety' ON (and separately Sequencer > 'Safety fail mode' > 'Fail Closed (Park)') immediately raised a red CRITICAL toast titled 'Safe the rig' reading 'CRITICAL: No weather data sources available. Rig safed: no action was possible.' An earlier variant also appended 'NO MOUNT CONNECTED -- nothing was parked; if a mount is ...'. Two problems: (1) a rig-SAFING event is being raised by a settings edit while nothing is running; (2) 'Rig safed' and 'no action was possible' are contradictory claims in one sentence -- nothing was safed because nothing was connected. I monitored for 5.5 minutes afterwards with fail-closed armed and it did NOT repeat, so this is a one-shot per state transition, not a flood.
expected: Changing a policy in Settings should surface an informational/warning disclosure ('Weather safety is on but no weather source is connected -- runs will park and abort with the current fail mode'), not a red CRITICAL safing alert. And the wording must not say the rig was safed when the app's own text says no action was possible.
repro: Fresh profile, nothing connected. Settings > AUTOMATION & SAFETY > Weather Safety > toggle 'Enable weather safety' ON. Screenshot within ~2s. Then Settings > Sequencer > 'Safety fail mode' > 'Fail Closed (Park)'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-07-ws-enabled.png (first, truncated variant), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-87-failclosed-toast.png (full text: 'Safe the rig / CRITICAL: No weather data sources available. Rig safed: no action was possible.'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-88-watch-1..6.png (no repeat over 5.5 min)
proposed_fix: Gate the SafeRig escalation on there being something to safe (a run in progress or a connected mount/dome); otherwise emit a warning-severity disclosure. And when detail resolves to 'no action was possible', drop the 'Rig safed:' lead-in entirely -- say 'Nothing to safe: no mount or dome connected.'
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim. Nothing connected (Camera/Mount/Guider all Disconnected), no run active, app parked on the Settings screen. Toggling Weather Safety > 'Enable weather safety' ON raised, within 2s, a red toast titled 'Safe the rig' reading 'CRITICAL: No weather data sources available. Rig safed: no action was possible. NO MOUNT CONNECTED - nothing was parked; if a mount is ...' (shot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sov-06-ws-on.png). Both cited locations are exact: safe_rig_service.dart:504 is literally `'CRITICAL: $reason. Rig safed: $detail.$gap'` with detail defaulting to 'no action was possible' at :498, and weather_safety_provider.dart:625-700 is the no-data fail-mode path that resolves to unsafe/shouldPark. It is not merely a message: the app log recorded 'Secondary rig stopped' at 2026-08-01T14:57:23Z, i.e. the safing routine really executed off a settings edit on an idle app. The self-contradiction ('Rig safed: no action was possible') is real. P2 is right - one-shot per state transition, no repeat, no equipment at risk here, but it trains operators to ignore the one alert class that must never be ignored.
